subject: RavenAI dedicated capacity: stress-play scenarios & SLO alignment
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir.p@ravenai.com>
To: chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com
Cc: ava.nguyen@ravenai.com, procure@ravenai.com
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Sizing kickoff: RavenAI prod commit planning (traffic profile + SLO)

Hi Chloe —

Thanks for taking this on. Quick summary of what we expect from the RavenAI production rollout starting mid-April:
- Typical user request: generation ~150–300 tokens; ~70% of calls return ~180 tokens on average.
- Expected steady-state: 25 requests/sec sustained (global peak windows routed to US)
- Peak microbursts: up to 95 requests/sec for ~6–12 minutes during business hour spikes and scheduled campaign triggers.
- We currently define our p95 latency SLO at 350ms for single-turn responses (we can relax p99 in exchange for lower cost).
- Regulatory: we need an on-prem-like private VPC deployment but dedicated fleet is preferred for predictable SLAs.

Can you share a mapping of tokens/sec to GPU count, recommended headroom (safety multiplier for microbursts), and a canary rollout plan? Procurement timeline: contracts signed by 23 Mar, deployment window 12–16 Apr.

Attachments: small CSV with RPS distribution (see attached).

—Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Platform
RavenAI
From: chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com
To: Samir Patel <samir.p@ravenai.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwoodinference.com, laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
Date: Fri, 27 Feb 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Sizing kickoff: RavenAI prod commit planning (traffic profile + SLO)

Samir — thanks for the clear profile. I ran an initial pass and sketched two commitment scenarios with math so we can align on risk vs cost. High-level conclusions first:
- Model baseline: assuming a 70B-class model quantized to 8-bit and inference stack tuned with KV caching and continuous batching, we estimate ~1,900 effective tokens/sec per H100-80GB GPU at 512 token context for our workload patterns.
- Required sustained tokens/sec (approx): 25 rps * 180 tokens = 4,500 tokens/sec. Peak microburst tokens/sec (95 rps * 180) = 17,100 tokens/sec.
- Option A (Conservative commit, minimal shared burst): 12x H100 dedicated -> theoretical capacity ~22,800 tokens/sec (12 * 1,900). Headroom vs peak ~1.33x. Good for p95=350ms with aggressive batching; minimal fallbacks.
- Option B (Cost-optimized with burst policy): 8x H100 dedicated (15,200 tokens/sec) + shared hosted burst for short microbursts. Headroom vs steady ~3.4x; vs peak bursts ~0.89x (requires hosted-tier bursting/fallback). Economical but needs robust fallback policy and routing.

Notes & assumptions (brief):
- Per-GPU number above assumes batching window <=25ms and average sequence lengths ~180 tokens; short-tail lower-latency traffic will have reduced batching benefit.
- We recommend planning for ~1.6x operating headroom on top of observed peak for scheduling and maintenance windows (so Option A effectively gives ~1.33x at the raw level but with ops cushion we like 1.6x target).
- Canary plan: start with 4 GPUs in the dedicated pool (canary subset of traffic, 5% of users) for 72 hours, measure p95/p99 and burst absorption, then scale to full commit in 48-hour increments. Automatic rollback to hosted fallback if p99 breaches 1.2s for more than 15 minutes.

I'll attach a quick workbook with the token->GPU math and a scenario chart. If you want I can loop in Karthik and Laura to pick the commercial slab.

Best,
Chloe Martin
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
To: Samir Patel <samir.p@ravenai.com>, chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com, karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 01 Mar 2026 08:42:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Sizing kickoff: RavenAI prod commit planning (traffic profile + SLO)

Samir / Chloe — quick commercial framing to pair with the technical options:
- Option A (12x H100): recommended if RavenAI wants SLA-backed latency & no dependence on hosted bursting. Pricing: monthly reserved slab at 18% discount vs on-demand; we can offer a 10% uplift credit if RavenAI signs a 12-month commit and agrees to the standard SLA with p95 350ms.
- Option B (8x H100 + burst): 25% lower monthly commit; includes an agreed burst floor (up to 30% of peak minutes per month) to be routed to shared pool. We'd need a documented fallback playbook and a 30-day trial of the burst behavior.

Commercial asks: if we aim to close by 23 Mar, please confirm which option you prefer and whether you want the trial window. We'll feed that into the DocuSign packet and the SLA schedule.

-Ben
Ben Carter
VP, Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Samir Patel <samir.p@ravenai.com>
To: ben.carter@redwoodinference.com, chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com
Cc: ava.nguyen@ravenai.com, procure@ravenai.com
Date: Tue, 02 Mar 2026 11:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Sizing kickoff: RavenAI prod commit planning (traffic profile + SLO)

Ben / Chloe — thanks. RavenAI prefers Option B (8x H100 + burst) for cost reasons, but we need the trial and a clear rollback policy (your canary approach sounds good). A few clarifying items:
- Can you quantify expected p99 under Option B during a 12-minute full-peak microburst if burst capacity is exhausted?
- Procurement: we need a 30-day trial included and acceptance criteria in the SLA doc. Can you add that to the DocuSign?
- Security: we'll need the private VPC option and a short onboarding checklist for KMS/HSM integration (Ava will own).

Procurement timeline: we'll review the packet on 15 Mar and plan to sign by 23 Mar if trial terms look good.

—Samir
From: chloe.martin@redwoodinference.com
To: Samir Patel <samir.p@ravenai.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwoodinference.com, laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com, karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com, ava.nguyen@ravenai.com
Date: Wed, 03 Mar 2026 16:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Sizing kickoff: RavenAI prod commit planning (traffic profile + SLO)

Samir — noted and confirmed Option B path. Quick answers and next steps below.

1) p99 expectation during exhausted-burst microburst:
- If dedicated pool (8x H100 -> ~15.2k tokens/sec) is saturated and hosted burst is unavailable, we expect p99 to degrade to ~1.2–1.6s for your average 180-token responses for a sustained multi-minute peak due to queuing and reduced batching efficiency. Shorter spikes (~<3 minutes) typically see p99 closer to ~700–900ms because batching recovers quickly. We'll surface exact numbers from the trial telemetry.

2) Trial & SLA additions:
- We'll include a 30-day trial window in the DocuSign packet and add acceptance criteria: baseline p95 <=350ms for 95% of hours during the trial, p99 <=1.5s for 95% of hours, and documented rollback steps if p99 >1.8s for >15 continuous minutes.

3) Security onboarding:
- Attached is a one-page KMS/HSM checklist and a list of required ACLs for the private VPC. Ava — can you and your security ops confirm the KMS provider and whether HSM-backed keys are mandatory?

4) Execution plan (short):
- Week of 12 Apr: deploy 8x H100 dedicated slab in customer VPC 
- 12–15 Apr: canary (4 GPUs) at 5% traffic -> validate metrics & tracing
- 16 Apr: ramp to 8 GPUs, enable burst routing for scheduled campaign windows, monitor for 72 hours
- 30 Apr: end of trial evaluation and go/no-go for 12-month reserved commit

I'll update the workbook and push the DocuSign with the trial clause and SLA language today. Looping Karthik for any final ops tolerances.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this greenlit.

Best,
Chloe
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
